name: sustained_accel_cv
reason: 24.2% finite, non-zero variance, strong separation (BEV 0.74 vs ICE 0.51, AUROC 0.71). Artefact check passed and acted on: decomposing a within phases into a 1-s moving average and a high-frequency residual shows the whole signal is in the smoothed envelope (AUROC 0.707) while the residual noise level is identical across powertrains (AUROC 0.505; median residual std 0.149 vs 0.140), so the feature is now computed on the 1-s smoothed trace (fixed) to exclude any aEgo quantisation/noise cue; raw and smoothed versions correlate 0.99.
rationale: Coefficient of variation (pooled std / pooled mean) of the 1-s smoothed longitudinal acceleration within sustained human acceleration phases (gas pressed >= 3 s, mean a >= 0.5 m/s^2, das_enabled == 0). It measures how flat the acceleration profile is while the driver holds the throttle: a single-speed BEV delivers an immediate torque peak that then decays with speed once power-limited (within-phase da/dv median -0.038 s^-1 for BEV vs +0.009 for ICE), giving a high CV, whereas an ICE builds torque with rpm and re-plateaus through gear changes, giving a flatter profile. Shift dips would add variance for stepped ICE gearboxes, but at 10 Hz the envelope decay dominates.
hypothesis: BEV > ICE (observed 0.74 vs 0.51); the pre-registered 'shift dips raise ICE CV' direction is reversed by the power-limited envelope decay. Size-neutral (observed rho +0.05).
audit_reason: The CV is a gas-flag duty-cycle measure, not the torque envelope: it correlates 0.86 with the share of phase samples at a < 0.2 m/s^2 (gas held through cruise in one-pedal cars; BEV phases last 109 vs 74 samples), truncating phases at the end of acceleration drops the AUROC from 0.71 to 0.59, and windows whose phases have < 10% low-acceleration tail show no separation (0.475). The pre-registered direction was reversed and the rationale rewritten post hoc to fit; the mechanism it really captures is already covered by direct one-pedal features.
